question: What immediate action should a midwife take if a loose nuchal cord is found around the baby's neck?

options.A: Pull hard on the shoulders to unwrap the cord
options.B: Gently slip the cord over the baby's head
options.C: Clamp and cut the cord immediately before the head is fully out
options.D: Push the baby back inside the uterus until the cord falls off

explanation: A loose cord can usually be looped over the fetal head without cutting it, provided there is enough slack. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T2#BMP212_U3_T2_h3)

question: Which finding during community ANC means a woman must be referred to a hospital immediately?

options.A: Normal physiological ankle swelling at the end of the day
options.B: Any amount of vaginal bleeding during pregnancy
options.C: Mild morning nausea experienced during the first trimester
options.D: A slight increase in appetite as the pregnancy progresses

explanation: Vaginal bleeding at any stage of pregnancy can indicate a serious life-threatening complication like placenta previa or abruption, requiring urgent hospital care. [learn more](BMP215_U2_T2#BMP215_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT something a midwife should do if parents refuse vitamin K?

options.A: Scolding the parents harshly for putting their baby at risk
options.B: Notifying the senior medical officer on duty about the case
options.C: Explaining the purpose and benefits of the medication again
options.D: Documenting the refusal clearly in the infant health record

explanation: Yelling at or scolding parents breaks trust and goes against professional conduct. Counseling must always remain respectful and calm. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T1#BMP213_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which statement shows that a midwife is using trauma-informed communication?

options.A: "You just need to forget the past and focus on your baby."
options.B: "If you had left earlier, you would not be in this situation."
options.C: "Why did you wait so long before coming to the clinic?"
options.D: "I believe you, and none of this is your fault."

explanation: Validating the survivor's experience and removing blame fosters trust and emotional safety. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T7#BMP310_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is BBT tracking alone limited when used by a couple trying to avoid pregnancy?

options.A: It increases the total number of days in the menstrual cycle
options.B: It stops working once a woman turns thirty years old
options.C: It only confirms ovulation after it has already occurred
options.D: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to read daily

explanation: Because BBT only shows that ovulation happened in the past, it does not give advance warning before the fertile window opens. [learn more](BMP224_U4_T4#BMP224_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary function of the Mental Health Review Tribunal?

options.A: To review involuntary detentions and protect patient liberty through independent hearings
options.B: To punish nurses who make charting errors in patient clinical notes
options.C: To manage the daily financial budget and purchase drugs for psychiatric wards
options.D: To hire and fire hospital directors across public health institutions

explanation: The tribunal provides an independent legal check to ensure patients are not wrongfully or excessively detained against their will. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T3#BMP223_U1_T3_h6)

question: A Nigerian nurse plans to migrate and practice abroad. Why are international educational standards helpful in this situation?

options.A: They automatically grant a license without further testing
options.B: They guarantee a higher salary in the destination country
options.C: They translate local Nigerian textbooks into foreign languages
options.D: They ensure basic competencies are recognized across borders

explanation: Common global standards make it easier for regulatory bodies to evaluate the training background of migrating nurses. [learn more](BMP110_U1_T6#BMP110_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why do patients with acute hepatitis often notice their urine becoming very dark like strong tea?

options.A: The patient is severely dehydrated from vomiting
options.B: Excess conjugated bilirubin spills over into the urine
options.C: White blood cells are being filtered through the kidneys
options.D: The kidneys are bleeding internally from the infection

explanation: As bilirubin accumulates in the blood, water-soluble conjugated bilirubin is excreted by the kidneys, darkening the urine color. [learn more](BMP125_U4_T1#BMP125_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which bone-building cells are stimulated by fluoride?

options.A: Fibroblasts
options.B: Osteoclasts
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: Osteoblasts

explanation: Osteoblasts are the cells that build bone, and fluoride helps stimulate their activity to strengthen bones. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T12#BMP118_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why do skeletal muscle fibers have more than one nucleus?

options.A: To allow the cell to survive if a single nucleus is damaged by lactic acid
options.B: To produce hormones that regulate blood calcium levels during contraction
options.C: Because they divide rapidly by mitosis whenever a muscle is injured
options.D: Because they fuse together from many smaller embryonic cells during development

explanation: During development, many smaller precursor cells join together to form a single long skeletal muscle fiber, leaving all of their nuclei inside the shared cell. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T8#BMP111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why do pregnant women clear more iodine through their kidneys?

options.A: Enlargement of the bladder pressing on the ureters
options.B: Frequent dehydration caused by morning sickness
options.C: Blockage of the renal tubules by high progesterone levels
options.D: Increased glomerular filtration rate in the kidneys

explanation: The kidneys filter blood much faster during pregnancy, leading to increased loss of various substances, including iodine. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T8#BMP212_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the name of the normal, harmless swelling that appears on a newborn's scalp after a ventouse delivery?

options.A: Chignon
options.B: Subgaleal hematoma
options.C: Cephalhematoma
options.D: Caput succedaneum

explanation: The chignon is the localized artificial swelling created by the vacuum cup that normally goes away quickly without treatment. [learn more](BMP311_U3_T2#BMP311_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why do viruses rely completely on host cells to survive?

options.A: They are too large to survive outside of human blood vessels
options.B: They can only reproduce when exposed to direct sunlight
options.C: They possess thick cell walls made of peptidoglycan
options.D: They completely lack their own metabolic machinery and energy production

explanation: Viruses do not have the cellular structures needed to make energy or proteins independently, forcing them to invade living cells. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T1#BMP116_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why are short video clips of labor mechanisms a helpful addition to a midwifery lecture?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any clinical hospital postings
options.B: They translate abstract descriptions into clear visual reality
options.C: They prove that textbooks are completely useless for students
options.D: They guarantee that students will never fail an exam

explanation: Videos allow students to see moving biological processes that can be hard to picture from static drawings or text. [learn more](BMP312_U3_T4#BMP312_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why is increasing dietary calcium and Vitamin D especially important for menopausal women?

options.A: To help combat accelerated bone mineral density loss
options.B: To prevent sudden spikes in daily blood pressure
options.C: To completely eliminate mild daytime hot flushes
options.D: To speed up sluggish thyroid hormone production

explanation: Lower oestrogen levels after menopause speed up bone breakdown, making adequate calcium and Vitamin D vital to prevent osteoporosis. [learn more](BMP320_U1_T5#BMP320_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To replace the need for physical abdominal examinations
options.B: To provide an early visual warning when labor becomes abnormal
options.C: To record only the medications given after delivery
options.D: To calculate the exact date and time of conception

explanation: The partograph is designed as a graphical tool to track labor progress and give early signals if something is going wrong. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h1)

question: When should skin-to-skin contact ideally start after a normal vaginal birth?

options.A: After the baby has received a bath
options.B: Only after the mother has slept for six hours
options.C: When the mother's mature milk comes in
options.D: Within the first hour of life

explanation: Placing the baby skin-to-skin right after birth helps them find the breast and keeps their temperature and blood sugar stable. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h2)

question: How does a full-term newborn usually react when you gently stroke their upper lip?

options.A: Turns the head sharply toward the opposite shoulder
options.B: Tilts the head backward and opens the mouth
options.C: Extends both arms upward in a startle motion
options.D: Sucks vigorously on the examiner's bare finger

explanation: Stroking the upper lip prompts the baby to tilt back slightly and open the mouth to take in the nipple. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h3)

question: A pregnant woman presents with severe anemia and exhaustion because her household culture dictates that men eat the most nutritious food first. Which factor is primarily at play?

options.A: An acute allergic reaction to standard antenatal iron supplements
options.B: Gender inequity affecting household nutritional distribution
options.C: A rare genetic blood disorder inherited from her parents
options.D: Natural physiological changes that occur in every normal pregnancy

explanation: Unequal food distribution based on gender roles directly deprives pregnant women of essential nutrients, leading to preventable conditions like severe anemia. [learn more](BMP310_U1_T3#BMP310_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is a common challenge when trying to introduce new research findings into a busy hospital?

options.A: An immediate ban on all forms of antenatal drugs
options.B: The requirement to write a textbook before starting work
options.C: A complete lack of pregnant women visiting the clinic
options.D: Resistance from staff accustomed to traditional routines

explanation: Healthcare staff often resist change because they are used to doing things a certain way, requiring good leadership to introduce new evidence. [learn more](BMP225_U1_T1#BMP225_U1_T1_h5)

question: How do adult tapeworms obtain their nourishment from the human host?

options.A: Swallowing red blood cells through a central mouth
options.B: Producing their own food via internal chemical organs
options.C: Chewing solid food particles using sharp mouthparts
options.D: Absorbing digested food straight through their skin

explanation: Tapeworms lack a digestive tract entirely, so they absorb nutrients directly across their outer body surface. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T8#BMP116_U3_T8_h2)

question: Who can be involved in antenatal nutritional counseling to help create a supportive home environment?

options.A: Traditional bone setters only
options.B: Hospital security personnel
options.C: Partners or family members
options.D: Pharmaceutical sales representatives

explanation: Involving household decision-makers helps ensure the pregnant woman receives practical support at home. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T16#BMP212_U1_T16_h6)

question: A couple visits a primary health centre after failing to conceive for two years. What is the best first step for the midwife?

options.A: Prescribe high-dose fertility hormones to the woman without testing
options.B: Advise them to separate for six months before seeking further help
options.C: Take a detailed joint history covering sexual habits and past infections
options.D: Immediately refer them to a tertiary fertility center for IVF treatment

explanation: Taking a thorough history helps spot lifestyle, infectious, or ovulation factors before jumping to advanced treatments. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T8#BMP126_U2_T8_h3)

question: In public health midwifery, what does a community mean beyond just houses on a street?

options.A: A collection of medical records kept in a primary health centre
options.B: A rigid administrative zone controlled only by local government
options.C: A temporary gathering of patients waiting inside a clinic
options.D: A dynamic network of people sharing values and health challenges

explanation: In public health, a community is defined by the shared connections, values, and health realities of the people living together, rather than just physical buildings. [learn more](BMP117_U2_T1#BMP117_U2_T1_h1)

question: How do immune complexes primarily damage the kidney during glomerulonephritis?

options.A: They destroy the bladder lining and travel upward to infect the renal tissue
options.B: They stop the bone marrow from producing normal red blood cells
options.C: They get trapped in the glomeruli and spark a damaging inflammatory response
options.D: They block the ureters completely and cause urine to back up into the kidneys

explanation: Circulating immune complexes lodge in the glomerular capillaries, causing white blood cells to rush in and damage the filtering membrane. [learn more](BMP216_U1_T4#BMP216_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main difference between beta-1 selective blockers and non-selective beta-blockers?

options.A: Beta-1 blockers target the heart, while non-selective blockers also affect the lungs
options.B: Beta-1 blockers are used only for pregnant women
options.C: Non-selective blockers only work on alpha receptors
options.D: Beta-1 blockers raise blood pressure while non-selective ones lower it

explanation: Beta-1 receptors are mostly found in the heart, so selective blockers act there. Non-selective blockers also affect beta-2 receptors in areas like the lungs. [learn more](BMP124_U2_T3#BMP124_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which pregnant woman attending an antenatal clinic needs the closest observation and is classified as high-risk?

options.A: A thirty-two-year-old woman in her first pregnancy with normal blood pressure
options.B: A twenty-eight-year-old woman carrying a single healthy fetus at twenty weeks
options.C: A twenty-two-year-old woman experiencing mild ankle swelling at thirty-four weeks
options.D: A twenty-five-year-old woman with a history of three previous spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: A history of recurrent pregnancy loss is a major risk factor that places a woman in a high-risk category requiring extra care. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h1)

question: What other physical sign is often seen with varicose veins in the lower legs?

options.A: Severe peeling skin rashes
options.B: Cold and pale toes
options.C: Ankle and foot swelling
options.D: Total loss of hair growth

explanation: Poor blood return causes fluid to leak into surrounding tissues, producing swelling around the ankles and feet. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T14#BMP212_U1_T14_h4)

question: When is the use of a mechanical lift mandatory for patient transfers?

options.A: Whenever a patient complains of mild morning fatigue
options.B: Only when visiting family members request special equipment
options.C: During every single routine blood pressure measurement
options.D: When the patient's weight exceeds safe manual lifting limits

explanation: Mechanical lifts are designed to protect staff from excessive load forces when patients cannot bear their own weight. [learn more](BMP110_U4_T6#BMP110_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which diagnostic imaging method is safest for checking a pregnant woman for a liver abscess?

options.A: Standard X-ray of the abdomen
options.B: Abdominal ultrasound
options.C: Computed tomography (CT)
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)

explanation: Ultrasound uses sound waves rather than ionizing radiation, making it safe and effective for evaluating hepatic lesions during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP116_U3_T5#BMP116_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the main focus of primary health care delivery?

options.A: Complex surgical procedures and treatments
options.B: Advanced medical research and trials
options.C: Preventive and promotive health services
options.D: Exclusive management of rare diseases

explanation: Primary health care focuses heavily on stopping illness before it starts through prevention and health promotion within communities. [learn more](BMP110_U2_T2#BMP110_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is a reliable source of clean water critical during home birth preparation?

options.A: To submerge the newborn infant immediately after delivery
options.B: For handwashing, linen cleaning, and maintaining infection control
options.C: For filling hot water bottles to warm the mother's feet
options.D: To mix herbal concoctions for accelerating active labor contractions

explanation: Clean water is vital for hand hygiene and washing equipment or linens to prevent postpartum infections. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T4#BMP215_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do bacteria in the genus Clostridium behave regarding oxygen?

options.A: They grow with or without oxygen
options.B: They cannot survive in oxygen
options.C: They need plenty of oxygen to grow
options.D: They need very little oxygen

explanation: Clostridium species are strict anaerobes, meaning they cannot survive or multiply in the presence of oxygen and need oxygen-free environments. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T8#BMP116_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is a midwife checking for when assessing Goodell sign?

options.A: Bluish color of the vagina
options.B: Compressibility of the lower uterus
options.C: Enlargement of the abdomen
options.D: Softening of the cervix

explanation: Goodell sign refers specifically to the softening of the cervical tissue resulting from increased vascularity and fluid retention. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T2#BMP212_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is sudden lowering of blood pressure (hypotension) a concern for a postpartum woman taking cabergoline?

options.A: The drug can lower blood pressure, adding to postpartum vulnerability to fainting.
options.B: It rapidly increases heart rate to dangerous levels during rest.
options.C: It triggers immediate allergic swelling in the legs.
options.D: It causes severe dehydration by locking fluid inside the kidneys.

explanation: Postpartum mothers are already prone to blood pressure shifts after delivery, and cabergoline can add to this risk, causing lightheadedness upon standing. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T8#BMP213_U4_T8_h4)

question: What happens when healthcare providers engage community elders in family health education?

options.A: Young people stop visiting the health facility altogether
options.B: The government reduces funding for rural primary health centers
options.C: Traditional birth attendants lose all their influence permanently
options.D: Community resistance to modern contraceptive services drops significantly

explanation: Involving respected traditional and community leaders builds local trust and removes cultural suspicion surrounding reproductive health. [learn more](BMP224_U2_T4#BMP224_U2_T4_h4)

question: A postpartum woman has normal blood pressure but her skin is pale, cool, and she feels very anxious. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: She has a sudden infection causing her skin temperature to drop
options.B: She is experiencing a normal reaction to the cold delivery room
options.C: Her heart has completely stopped pumping blood to her lungs
options.D: Her body is compensating for blood loss by constricting blood vessels

explanation: Compensatory mechanisms keep blood pressure stable temporarily while shunting blood away from the skin, causing pallor and coolness. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T3#BMP110_U7_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of an experimental research design in healthcare?

options.A: To collect personal opinions through long interviews
options.B: To list the frequency of diseases in a specific state
options.C: To show a direct cause-and-effect relationship
options.D: To observe people in their natural habitats without changing anything

explanation: Experimental designs are built specifically to test whether an intervention causes a specific outcome by actively introducing a change. [learn more](BMP225_U2_T4#BMP225_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is a non-judgmental attitude from midwives especially important when caring for pregnant teenagers?

options.A: It encourages young girls to attend antenatal clinics early and seek help without fear
options.B: It guarantees that the teenager will experience a completely painless labor
options.C: It prevents the teenager from ever engaging in sexual activity again
options.D: It legally protects the hospital from being sued by community leaders

explanation: Adolescents often fear scolding or harsh treatment from healthcare workers; a welcoming approach builds trust and ensures they return for vital care. [learn more](BMP320_U3_T2#BMP320_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is the absolute first priority when arriving at an emergency scene?

options.A: Ensuring scene safety
options.B: Calling the police
options.C: Checking the pulse rate
options.D: Administering oxygen

explanation: You must check the environment for hazards first so you do not become a victim yourself. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T9#BMP110_U7_T9_h2)

question: What is the main structural job of the intrinsic foot muscles?

options.A: Providing heavy power for running fast
options.B: Extending the knee during walking
options.C: Supporting the arches of the foot
options.D: Rotating the hip joint outward

explanation: Intrinsic muscles act like tiny stabilizing cables that maintain the arches of the foot and assist with delicate toe movements. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T11#BMP111_U3_T11_h5)

question: A village elder is hesitant to let pregnant women visit the clinic due to custom. What is best to do first?

options.A: Report him to the police for obstructing essential public health services
options.B: Threaten to cut off all government food supplies to his household
options.C: Ignore his authority completely and open the clinic doors anyway
options.D: Approach him respectfully to discuss the health risks and build a shared solution

explanation: Respectful dialogue builds trust and helps leaders see the project as a shared benefit rather than a challenge to their authority. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h3)

question: A patient on tuberculosis treatment reports that their urine has turned bright orange and wants to stop taking the drugs. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Suggest drinking large amounts of palm oil to flush out the colored substance
options.B: Explain that this is a normal, harmless side effect of rifampicin and treatment must continue
options.C: Tell the patient to switch to taking only herbal remedies instead
options.D: Advise the patient to stop all medications immediately and come to the clinic

explanation: Reassuring the patient prevents unwarranted discontinuation of a life-saving medication regimen. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of postoperative dietary management after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To encourage rapid weight gain through high-protein solid meals
options.B: To prevent dehydration by forcing large amounts of dairy products
options.C: To stimulate immediate bowel evacuation within twelve hours
options.D: To minimize bowel movements and protect the surgical repair site

explanation: Low-residue diets and softeners reduce stool frequency and bulk, preventing undue strain on the newly repaired tissues. [learn more](BMP310_U3_T11#BMP310_U3_T11_h5)

question: A clinic has well-trained staff, but all malaria medications are out of stock. Which IMCI pillar is failing here?

options.A: Family and community practices
options.B: Nutritional rehabilitation tracking
options.C: Health systems strengthening
options.D: Case management skill development

explanation: Drug supply chain management and facility readiness fall directly under the health systems strengthening pillar of IMCI. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in the antenatal ward speaks extremely fast, interrupts staff constantly, and believes she is destined to lead the nation. What clinical state does this suggest?

options.A: A manic episode
options.B: Severe iron-deficiency fatigue
options.C: Normal pregnancy anxiety
options.D: A standard postpartum blues reaction

explanation: Pressured speech combined with grandiose beliefs about ruling the nation strongly indicates acute mania. [learn more](BMP223_U3_T2#BMP223_U3_T2_h2)

question: What does frequency mean in a statistical table?

options.A: The time between hospital shifts
options.B: The largest number in a data set
options.C: How many times a value appears
options.D: The average weight of a newborn

explanation: Frequency simply counts the number of times a particular observation or score occurs in your data set. [learn more](BMP225_U4_T2#BMP225_U4_T2_h2)

question: A midwife walks in to check a tired mother on the ward. What is the best first step?

options.A: Greet the mother warmly, introduce yourself, and explain what you will do
options.B: Undress the newborn baby quickly while the mother is resting
options.C: Immediately check the perineal pad without asking for permission
options.D: Record vital signs on the chart before speaking to anyone in the room

explanation: Building trust and asking permission helps the mother feel relaxed and comfortable with your care. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is a common early sign of low calcium levels during pregnancy?

options.A: Sudden weight loss
options.B: Excessive hair growth
options.C: Painful muscle cramps
options.D: Yellowing of the eyes

explanation: Low calcium affects the nerves and muscles, often showing up as painful spasms or cramps in the legs and feet. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T6#BMP118_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why does poor hand hygiene increase biological hazard risks in a maternity unit?

options.A: It attracts mosquitoes and other flying insects into the ward
options.B: It neutralizes the effectiveness of hospital soap and water
options.C: It allows microbes to transfer easily between patients and staff
options.D: It causes the skin on the hands to become dry and peel off

explanation: Hands act as vehicles for transmitting infectious agents. Washing and sanitizing hands break the chain of infection in clinical settings. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T2#BMP126_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main problem that happens in the body during obstetric shock?

options.A: Rapid destruction of platelets in the blood
options.B: Sudden rise in pressure inside the head
options.C: Not enough blood flow reaching vital organs
options.D: Complete stopping of kidney filtering

explanation: Shock happens when the circulatory system fails to supply enough blood and oxygen to vital organs, causing cells to stop working properly. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard routine laboratory test during an initial ANC visit?

options.A: Hemoglobin or packed cell volume
options.B: Urinalysis for protein and glucose
options.C: Liver biopsy
options.D: HIV screening

explanation: Liver biopsies are complex, invasive surgical procedures never done as routine antenatal screening at a primary health care clinic. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T2#BMP126_U1_T2_h2)

question: What should a midwife do if a patient is too weak to cough up sputum?

options.A: Collect ordinary saliva and label it as sputum
options.B: Wait several days until the patient regains strength
options.C: Scrape the back of the patient's throat with a cotton swab
options.D: Consult the medical officer for assistance like nebulized saline or physiotherapy

explanation: Weak patients often need clinical support like nebulization or physical therapy to help clear respiratory secretions. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T4#BMP110_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why do midwives check the baby's leg movements during an initial assessment for spina bifida?

options.A: To check if the baby is experiencing neonatal jaundice
options.B: To calculate the exact birth weight of the infant
options.C: To estimate the level and severity of spinal nerve damage
options.D: To determine if the infant needs immediate cardiac surgery

explanation: Checking movement and muscle tone in the legs helps clinicians understand which nerve roots are working below the spinal defect. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T4#BMP220_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the typical microscopic shape and arrangement of Neisseria species?

options.A: Gram-positive clusters
options.B: Gram-positive bacilli
options.C: Gram-negative diplococci
options.D: Acid-fast spirochaetes

explanation: Neisseria species appear under the microscope as pairs of round cells that stain negative with crystal violet. [learn more](BMP116_U2_T5#BMP116_U2_T5_h1)

question: How does morphine manage to reach the unborn baby after maternal administration?

options.A: By absorbing via the maternal skin pores
options.B: By crossing the placental barrier
options.C: By diffusing directly through the amniotic sac
options.D: By traveling through the fallopian tubes

explanation: Because of its chemical properties, morphine readily passes from the mother's blood vessels through the placenta into the fetal circulation. [learn more](BMP213_U2_T2#BMP213_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which cranial nerve carries the touch signals that trigger a baby's rooting reflex?

options.A: Trigeminal nerve
options.B: Facial nerve
options.C: Vagus nerve
options.D: Hypoglossal nerve

explanation: The trigeminal nerve supplies feeling to the face, picking up the touch on the cheek or lip during rooting. [learn more](BMP214_U1_T5#BMP214_U1_T5_h2)

question: What feature of the tonsils helps increase their surface area to catch incoming germs?

options.A: Mucosal cilia
options.B: Fibrous capsules
options.C: Secretory ducts
options.D: Tonsillar crypts

explanation: Deep folds called tonsillar crypts create a large surface area where foreign particles and bacteria get trapped so immune cells can find them. [learn more](BMP111_U6_T4#BMP111_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why does the IMCI protocol focus on looking at the whole child rather than just treating a single disease?

options.A: It is a requirement for receiving free prescription drugs from donors.
options.B: Laboratory facilities are always fully available in primary health centers.
options.C: Specialist pediatricians are stationed at every rural clinic in the country.
options.D: Sick children often present with multiple overlapping and interconnected conditions.

explanation: Children rarely present with just one isolated problem, so addressing all symptoms at once saves lives. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T9#BMP222_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which mineral is mainly responsible for regulating fluid volume outside of cells?

options.A: Magnesium
options.B: Potassium
options.C: Sodium
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Sodium is the major mineral outside the cells that dictates water distribution and overall fluid balance in the body. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T13#BMP118_U2_T13_h3)

question: How do dietary fibers help protect adults against type 2 diabetes?

options.A: By completely blocking the stomach from digesting any carbohydrates
options.B: By increasing the body's daily requirement for physical rest
options.C: By slowing down the digestion and absorption of glucose into the bloodstream

options.B: To block all sensory nerve pathways coming from the pelvis

question: When does kwashiorkor most commonly develop in young Nigerian children?

options.D: During the exclusive breastfeeding period

question: What is the main job of the fibrin mesh formed during the clotting stage?

options.C: To prevent white blood cells from reaching the wound
options.D: To permanently replace damaged skin cells instantly

explanation: Fibrin creates a tight web that reinforces the fragile platelet plug to properly stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T2#BMP120_U3_T2_h3)

question: How does fair duty rostering relate directly to the staffing management function?

options.C: It balances workloads and helps prevent staff burnout

question: Which of the following is a primary reproductive health need for young adolescents?

options.A: Advanced fertility treatments
options.B: Routine geriatric screenings
options.C: Safe menstrual hygiene management
options.D: Immediate planning for menopause

explanation: Managing menstruation safely with proper education and materials is a fundamental health need for adolescent girls as they enter puberty. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T9#BMP126_U2_T9_h2)

question: When should a midwife expect to use empiric antimicrobial therapy?

options.A: Only after all laboratory test results are fully confirmed
options.B: At the very end of a failed course of narrow-spectrum treatment
options.C: When the patient shows an allergy to standard first-line drugs
options.D: Before laboratory culture and sensitivity results are ready

explanation: Empiric treatment starts right away based on clinical signs and common local germs while waiting for lab tests to confirm the exact cause. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T1#BMP124_U4_T1_h1)

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the ADME acronym of pharmacokinetics?

options.A: Movement
options.B: Metabolism
options.C: Monitoring
options.D: Malformation

explanation: In pharmacokinetics, metabolism refers to the chemical breakdown or alteration of drugs by the body, mainly in the liver. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T1#BMP124_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary causative agent of tuberculosis?

options.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Klebsiella pneumoniae
options.D: Bordetella pertussis

explanation: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which typically targets the respiratory system. [learn more](BMP125_U1_T7#BMP125_U1_T7_h1)

question: What are the two main pillars at the heart of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Hospital expansion and funding
options.B: Technology and advanced research
options.C: Specialized curative medicine
options.D: Social justice and equity

explanation: Primary Health Care is built on ensuring fair distribution and equal access to health services for all people. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is immediate contraceptive counseling important following a complete abortion?

options.A: Fertility can return as early as two weeks after the event

options.C: Women are legally required to wait two years before conceiving
options.D: Pregnancy is biologically impossible for a full year afterward

explanation: Ovulation can resume very quickly after a miscarriage, so patients need birth control guidance right away if they wish to avoid immediate pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T4#BMP221_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which past surgery is especially critical to note because it increases the risk of uterine rupture?

options.A: Tonsillectomy done five years ago
options.B: Appendectomy performed during childhood
options.C: Previous myomectomy or caesarean section
options.D: Repair of a simple hand laceration

explanation: Surgeries that cut into the muscular wall of the uterus weaken the tissue, raising the risk that the uterus could rupture during a future labour. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) during community outbreaks?

options.A: It completely cures children who already show signs of severe paralysis
options.B: It requires refrigeration storage that is much easier to maintain than IPV
options.C: It builds gut immunity that helps stop the person-to-person spread of the virus
options.D: It destroys bacteria in drinking water sources across rural villages

explanation: OPV creates strong local immunity in the intestine, which prevents the wild virus from multiplying and spreading in the community. [learn more](BMP222_U2_T8#BMP222_U2_T8_h5)

question: What does a severe degree of skull bone molding (+3) typically suggest during a difficult labor?

options.A: Significant compression of the fetal head trying to pass through a tight pelvis
options.B: An unusually high volume of clear amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus
options.C: Early rupture of the amniotic membranes before the onset of contractions
options.D: Normal rapid descent of the baby without any mechanical obstruction

explanation: High molding scores show that the baby's skull bones are overlapping heavily to fit through a potentially narrow birth canal. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why must midwives be cautious when relying solely on clinical physical exams for nutrition?

options.A: Pregnant women never display physical symptoms of poor nutrition
options.B: Physical examinations are illegal for midwives to perform in primary care clinics
options.C: Physical signs usually only show up when a nutrient deficiency is already quite advanced
options.D: Clinical signs are identical for every single vitamin deficiency known to science

explanation: Clinical signs are late indicators, meaning the deficiency has already worsened inside the body by the time you see it. [learn more](BMP118_U4_T1#BMP118_U4_T1_h4)

question: How should a midwife shape their hand when entering the cervix for a manual removal of the placenta?

options.A: Spread out with fingers apart
options.B: Clenched into a hard fist
options.C: Flattened like a paddle
options.D: Formed into a tight cone shape

explanation: Shaping the hand into a cone reduces trauma and helps it slide smoothly through the partially open cervix. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which physical sign on a newborn points toward a hidden or submucous cleft palate?

options.A: Extra fingers on both hands
options.B: A webbed neck
options.C: An absent clavicle
options.D: A bifid uvula

explanation: A split or bifid uvula is a classic visible sign that often indicates an underlying submucous cleft beneath the tissue of the palate. [learn more](BMP220_U2_T5#BMP220_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which local Nigerian food group provides the most easily absorbed source of phosphorus?

options.A: Raw cassava and unpeeled yam
options.B: Processed white flour pastries
options.C: Animal proteins like fish and meat
options.D: Sugary carbonated beverages

explanation: Animal sources provide phosphorus that the body can easily absorb and use without interference from plant compounds. [learn more](BMP118_U2_T7#BMP118_U2_T7_h3)

question: How do macrolides destroy bacteria without harming human cells?

options.A: Stomach acid destroys the drug before it reaches organs
options.B: Human skin blocks the drug from entering blood vessels
options.C: White blood cells quickly neutralize the antibiotic molecules
options.D: Human cells have structurally different ribosomal subunits

explanation: Because human ribosomes are different in size and composition from bacterial ribosomes, macrolides leave human cells alone. [learn more](BMP124_U4_T4#BMP124_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the key difference between prolonged labor and obstructed labor?

options.A: Uterine contractions completely stop before obstruction happens
options.B: Contractions are strong and regular in obstruction despite no fetal descent
options.C: Obstructed labor only occurs during the first stage of labor
options.D: Prolonged labor always causes immediate uterine rupture

explanation: Even though the uterus is working hard with strong contractions, a physical block prevents the baby from moving down. [learn more](BMP311_U2_T3#BMP311_U2_T3_h1)

question: How does an hourglass contraction of the uterus prevent a separated placenta from coming out?

options.A: It forces the placenta to implant deeper into the cervix.
options.B: It causes severe maternal hypertension.
options.C: It traps the placenta behind a closed lower uterine segment.
options.D: It dissolves the umbilical cord tissue prematurely.

explanation: An hourglass contraction is a muscle spasm in the lower uterine segment that physically blocks the placenta from exiting. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h1)

question: A pregnant woman with chronic hypertension is most at risk of developing which condition?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: Complete placenta previa
options.D: Superimposed preeclampsia

explanation: Chronic hypertension significantly raises the likelihood that a woman will develop preeclampsia later in her pregnancy. [learn more](BMP221_U3_T3#BMP221_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of physiological jaundice?

options.A: Normal feeding and active behavior
options.B: Gradual daily rise in bilirubin levels
options.C: Appearance within the first 12 hours of life
options.D: Resolution within two weeks of birth

explanation: Appearance within the first 12 hours is extremely early and classifies the jaundice as pathological, not physiological. [learn more](BMP220_U1_T6#BMP220_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is a reason a midwife must NOT insert a levonorgestrel IUCD?

options.A: Desire to have more children later
options.B: Mild primary dysmenorrhea
options.C: History of primary school education
options.D: Current confirmed pregnancy

explanation: An IUCD should never be inserted if the client is already pregnant, as it poses serious risks to both the pregnancy and the mother. [learn more](BMP224_U3_T9#BMP224_U3_T9_h2)

question: A midwife has just assisted with a manual removal of the placenta. What should be done next in the immediate post-procedure phase?

options.A: Check uterine tone and monitor vital signs every 15 minutes
options.B: Encourage immediate heavy ambulation around the ward
options.C: Discharge the patient home after one hour of rest
options.D: Remove the intravenous line to allow the mother to sleep

explanation: Close monitoring of vital signs and uterine contraction during the first hour helps catch hemorrhage and atony early. [learn more](BMP311_U4_T3#BMP311_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which of these points is most important when teaching a patient about maintenance medication for Crohn's disease?

options.A: Stop taking all prescription drugs as soon as abdominal pain stops
options.B: Switch to herbal remedies if the pharmacy runs out of stock
options.C: Double the medication dose whenever eating a high-fiber meal
options.D: Continue taking medications consistently even during periods of remission

explanation: Maintenance medications keep the immune system stable, so stopping them just because symptoms disappear often leads to a sudden flare-up. [learn more](BMP125_U3_T11#BMP125_U3_T11_h8)

question: Why is turning your back on an open sterile tray considered a breach of technique?

options.A: The sterile items will automatically cool down and attract moisture
options.B: Air currents from behind travel faster and carry heavy bacteria
options.C: You can no longer monitor it to ensure it remains uncontaminated
options.D: Hospital regulations require midwives to face instrument trays at all times

explanation: Unwatched sterile fields can easily be accidentally touched or contaminated by passing colleagues or movement without your knowledge. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T3#BMP120_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why is engagement impossible when a fetus is in a transverse lie at term?

options.A: The fetal head is too small to stimulate contractions
options.B: The placenta blocks the lower uterine segment entirely
options.C: The amniotic fluid volume is always too low
options.D: The broad shoulder cannot fit through the pelvic inlet

question: What is the primary focus of health promotion in midwifery practice?

options.A: Treating advanced infectious diseases with antibiotics
options.B: Writing policy guidelines for national health ministries
options.C: Performing emergency surgical procedures in the ward
options.D: Enabling people to increase control over their health

explanation: Health promotion is fundamentally about empowering individuals and communities to take charge of their own well-being and health determinants. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T2#BMP117_U3_T2_h1)

question: What is the best way for a midwife to handle vaccine hesitancy in a rural community?

options.A: Ignoring community concerns and forcing children to be vaccinated
options.B: Engaging local leaders and providing culturally sensitive health education
options.C: Stopping outreach clinics until community members ask for help
options.D: Threatening parents with legal action if they miss clinic days

explanation: Partnering with respected community figures and educating families patiently helps build trust and overcome fears or misconceptions. [learn more](BMP117_U3_T3#BMP117_U3_T3_h7)

question: At what gestational age is a planned cervical cerclage usually put in place?

options.A: 12 to 14 weeks
options.B: 38 to 40 weeks
options.C: 6 to 8 weeks
options.D: 28 to 30 weeks

explanation: A preventative cerclage is usually scheduled near the end of the first trimester, before the cervix has a chance to start changing. [learn more](BMP221_U1_T10#BMP221_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which of the following conditions involves blocked sebaceous ducts leading to trapped oil under the skin?

options.A: Psoriasis plaques
options.B: Atopic eczema
options.C: Contact dermatitis
options.D: Sebaceous cysts

explanation: A sebaceous cyst forms when a gland or its duct gets blocked, allowing sebum to build up into a smooth lump under the skin. [learn more](BMP111_U4_T10#BMP111_U4_T10_h5)

question: Why should midwives worry about severe, untreated anxiety during pregnancy?

options.A: It always causes high blood pressure
options.B: It stops the placenta from making progesterone
options.C: It damages the baby's brain structure
options.D: It can lead to preterm birth and low birth weight

explanation: High levels of ongoing stress and anxiety during pregnancy are linked to early delivery and smaller babies. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T4#BMP223_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why are large, charged molecules unable to cross the cell membrane by simple diffusion?

options.A: They are too light to stay on the surface of the cell
options.B: The cell membrane actively destroys charged particles
options.C: The interior of the phospholipid bilayer is hydrophobic
options.D: They dissolve completely in the extracellular fluid

question: After administering an intervention for low blood sugar, when should the midwife recheck the newborn's blood glucose?

question: Why is mental flexibility and adaptability important for a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: They rarely work with patients and spend most of their time doing research

question: What type of slide is recommended at the very start of a health education presentation?

question: How do surviving nephrons react when a large part of the kidney is damaged?

options.C: They stop producing urine to conserve water
options.D: They shut down completely to rest and heal

question: A woman bleeds heavily right after delivery, but abdominal palpation shows the uterus is firmly contracted. Which T is the most likely cause?

question: In routine postnatal care, which aspect is traditionally prioritized over mental health?

question: What dangerous complication can happen if you pull on the umbilical cord without pushing the uterus upward?

question: A newborn delivered at home is limp, pale, and not breathing even after drying and stimulation. What is the immediate action?

question: What is an important nursing duty when caring for a patient with a suspected clostridial infection?

question: What is another common name for parasympathomimetic drugs?

question: How should a midwife respond to a community member who believes female sterilization causes mental illness?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated maternal anemia?

options.B: Macrosomia

question: What kind of germ causes chlamydia?

question: What is the main goal of antenatal triage when women arrive at the clinic?

question: What is the main goal of prescribing cyclic progestins to a patient who does not ovulate regularly?

question: What happens to skin blood vessels when the body needs to release excess heat?

question: What is a major threat to the long-term survival of a community transport scheme?

question: What is the primary reason for running tests to check thyroid function when evaluating a patient with severe mood and energy changes?

question: Without medical intervention, when is an HIV-positive mother most likely to pass the virus to her baby?

question: What can happen if a urine sample is left sitting at room temperature for hours before reaching the lab?

options.C: The chemical composition of the urine freezes and solidifies

explanation: Leaving urine out too long allows bacteria to grow and white blood cells to break down, which ruins the accuracy of the test. [learn more](BMP110_U6_T6#BMP110_U6_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is a classic sign of myxedema coma?

question: Why are drugs like Mebendazole considered relatively safe during the second and third trimesters?

question: Which sign helps a midwife tell placental abruption apart from placenta praevia?

question: What is the specific emergency treatment used for severe heart collapse caused by local anaesthetic toxicity?

options.D: Normal saline solution

question: What is the main functional unit of the kidney that filters blood and makes urine?

question: Which specific cells inside the testes make testosterone?

question: Why do public health workers always teach water, sanitation, and hygiene together?

options.C: It is impossible to build a borehole without proper sanitation structures first

question: Why should a pregnant woman empty her bladder right before an abdominal check?

options.C: Urine samples are needed for every single physical check

question: What distinguishes postpartum psychosis from postpartum blues?

options.C: Presence of severe symptoms like hallucinations and detachment from reality
options.D: Mild sadness that disappears after a single good night of sleep

question: A midwife notices a colleague wrote a rude comment about a teenage mother in the case notes. What is the best action to take?

options.B: Tear out the affected page so nobody else reads the comment
options.C: Advise the colleague to use professional, objective language instead
options.D: Ignore the note since it does not affect the baby's vital signs

explanation: Midwifery notes must remain professional and free of personal bias, requiring peer correction when inappropriate language is used. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is a primary duty of a midwife during the postnatal period?

options.A: Assessing uterine involution and checking lochia
options.B: Administering chemotherapy for gestational trophoblastic disease
options.C: Fitting permanent contraceptive implants like tubal ligation
options.D: Performing major abdominal surgery for fibroids

explanation: Checking how the uterus contracts and monitoring lochia are standard postnatal assessments to ensure the mother is recovering safely after childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h2)

question: What does a foul, offensive odor in the lochia discharge typically indicate?

options.A: Standard hormonal shifts following lactation
options.B: An active intrauterine or endometrial infection
options.C: Normal progress of physiological tissue breakdown
options.D: Rapid healing of a superficial perineal tear

explanation: A foul odor indicates bacterial multiplication within the uterine cavity, signaling potential postpartum sepsis. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T1#BMP212_U4_T1_h5)

question: An HIV-positive mother with a low viral load just delivered a healthy baby. What is the priority action for the midwifery team?

options.A: Withholding all early feeding for forty-eight hours
options.B: Isolating the infant in a specialized nursery
options.C: Bathing the newborn in antiseptic solutions
options.D: Administering infant antiretroviral prophylaxis

explanation: Giving the baby early antiretroviral medicine helps clear out any virus they might have been exposed to during birth. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T5#BMP116_U4_T5_h5)

question: How many hours to the right of the alert line is the action line placed on the standard partograph?

options.A: 4 hours
options.B: 6 hours
options.C: 8 hours
options.D: 2 hours

explanation: The action line is positioned exactly four hours to the right of the alert line to allow a clear window for warning before decisive intervention is mandatory. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T6#BMP212_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why does the body naturally lower its BMR during periods of prolonged starvation?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of remaining food in the gut
options.B: To prepare the thyroid gland for producing extra hormones
options.C: To conserve energy and protect vital life-sustaining functions
options.D: To increase the rate at which proteins are built in muscles

explanation: Starvation triggers a survival mechanism where the body slows down its metabolic engine to make limited energy reserves last longer. [learn more](BMP118_U1_T4#BMP118_U1_T4_h4)

question: A midwife working to improve poor hospital lighting and staff shortages in her unit is addressing which category of the ICM code?

options.A: Professional Obligations only
options.B: Midwifery Practice alone
options.C: The Midwife's Practice Environment
options.D: Personal Financial Management

explanation: Working conditions, safety, and operational resources fall directly under the practice environment category of the ethical code. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why are people living with HIV at a higher risk of developing virus-induced cancers?

options.A: A weakened immune system fails to clear secondary viral infections
options.B: The virus produces toxins that destroy tumor suppressors
options.C: HIV turns every human organ into a tumor
options.D: Antiretroviral drugs cause rapid cell growth

explanation: A depleted immune system cannot control other viruses, allowing cancer-linked strains to multiply and transform host cells. [learn more](BMP116_U4_T4#BMP116_U4_T4_h4)
